stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition client running Minecraft 1.4.1 in a singleplayer Creative-mode world. Use keyboard and mouse controls, with the game and operating-system audio output audible. No seed, coordinates, multiplayer server, commands, resource pack, or special graphics setting is required by the report.
preconditions: Install and select the exact historical version Minecraft 1.4.1; do not use fix version 23w18a or a newer version for this reproduction.
Disable mods and custom movement modifications that could change player collision, sneaking, or walking behavior.
Use a Creative-mode world so an elevated test walkway can be constructed deterministically without gathering materials or risking survival damage.
Ensure the game Sound setting and the computer's audio output are high enough for the observation subsystem to inspect ordinary footstep audio.
Use an area with enough open space to build a one-block-wide elevated walkway with air beside its long edges.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation whose version is exactly Minecraft 1.4.1, then start the game with that installation. Do not substitute Minecraft 1.4.2 or any later affected version unless Minecraft 1.4.1 cannot be launched in the available environment.
steps.exact_input: Launcher installation version: Minecraft 1.4.1; click Play
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running client as Minecraft 1.4.1.

steps.action: Open the singleplayer world list, create a new world, and set its game mode to Creative. The world name, seed, and world type may remain at their defaults because the report supplies no required world generation settings.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new world has loaded, the Creative inventory is available, and the player can fly by double-tapping the jump control.

steps.action: Pause the game and make footstep audio easy to inspect. Set the game's Sound volume to an audible level, preferably 100%, and reduce Music to 0% so music does not mask short footstep sounds. Resume the world afterward.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options... -> Sound: 100%; Music: 0% -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The world is active again, game sound output is enabled, and background music will not mask the test.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory control, whose default key is E. Select a full solid block with an easily recognizable footstep sound, such as Wooden Planks, place a stack in the hotbar, and close the inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E; select Wooden Planks; place the stack in a hotbar slot; E or Esc to close
steps.success_cue: A stack of Wooden Planks or another full solid block is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the building block. If needed, double-tap the jump control, whose default key is Space, to begin Creative flight. Move to an open area where the test structure will not connect to trees, buildings, or terrain along either long side.
steps.exact_input: Press the hotbar number for the block stack; double-tap Space if flight is needed
steps.success_cue: The building block is shown in the player's hand and there is open space available for an elevated walkway.

steps.action: Using right-click to place blocks, construct a straight walkway that is exactly one full block wide and at least twelve blocks long. Put its top surface at least three blocks above the surrounding ground. A temporary pillar may be used to place the first block. Keep both long sides of the walkway unobstructed so that the block horizontally beyond either edge is air at the player's feet level.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place a 1-block-wide, at-least-12-block-long elevated row of blocks
steps.success_cue: A straight elevated walkway exists with a continuous level top, at least twelve blocks of usable length, and open air immediately beside both long edges.

steps.action: Land on the top surface near one end of the walkway, leaving at least eight blocks of walkway ahead. Stand near the center of the block width rather than at an edge. If flying, descend using the sneak control, whose default key is Left Shift, until the player is standing rather than flying.
steps.exact_input: Move above the walkway; hold Left Shift to descend; release it after landing
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the walkway, is not flying, and has at least eight blocks of straight walkway ahead.

steps.action: Turn so the player's forward direction points along the walkway's long axis. The crosshair should point toward the far end, not toward either open side. This orientation allows forward movement to remain parallel to the edge during the trigger.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until facing directly along the walkway
steps.success_cue: Pressing W would move the player along the length of the walkway rather than off its side.

steps.action: Switch to a third-person camera so the player's overhang can be inspected. In Minecraft 1.4.1, use the perspective-toggle control, whose default key is F5, until the player model and the relevant side edge of the walkway are visible.
steps.exact_input: F5
steps.success_cue: The player model is visible on screen and its position relative to the walkway edge can be judged.

steps.action: Hold the sneak control, whose default key is Left Shift. While continuing to hold it, use short taps of the sideways movement key that moves toward one open side of the walkway—A for the player's left or D for the player's right. Continue until sneak edge protection prevents any farther outward movement. Do not use W or S during this alignment.
steps.exact_input: Hold Left Shift; repeatedly tap A or D toward the selected open edge
steps.success_cue: The player remains supported by the walkway but is at the maximum sneaking overhang, with most of the player model extending beyond the selected side edge and the player's center visually over the adjacent air.

steps.action: Release the sideways movement key first, then release Left Shift without pressing another movement key. Do not turn the camera or move inward. If the player falls, return to the walkway and repeat the previous step using smaller sideways taps; the required starting state is a non-sneaking player still supported at the extreme edge.
steps.exact_input: Release A or D; then release Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The player is no longer sneaking, remains standing on the walkway, and retains the extreme outward offset with the center of the player over the air beside the walkway.

steps.action: Without pressing Left Shift and without steering inward, press and hold the forward movement control, whose default key is W, to begin ordinary walking parallel to the walkway's long edge. Keep the same outward offset and begin the movement before reaching the end of the walkway. This first non-sneaking walking movement while the player's center is over adjacent air is the trigger action.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold W
steps.success_cue: The player has begun moving lengthwise along the walkway while remaining supported at the extreme side edge; the reproduction setup is now ready for immediate footstep-effect observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just started ordinary, non-sneaking forward movement parallel to the elevated walkway while retaining the maximum outward overhang, with the player's center over the air beside the supporting blocks. Hand control to the observation subsystem for the remainder of this edge traversal.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal numbered Steps to Reproduce, so this plan reconstructs the minimum path from the original description's walking-at-the-edge example.

The first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.4.1, is selected as required. Historical launcher or Java-runtime compatibility may prevent that version from launching in some environments; if so, record the failure rather than silently selecting a later version.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, game mode, or test block. Creative mode, an elevated walkway, and Wooden Planks are practical choices used to create a deterministic edge with adjacent air and clearly distinguishable footstep audio.
The report does not supply an exact coordinate for the player-center threshold in Minecraft 1.4.1. The maximum-sneak-overhang procedure is used to establish that position manually.

The report describes several manifestations introduced in later versions, but blocks such as slime, honey, magma, and sculk sensors are not used because the recommended first affected version predates them.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition release 1.4.2 in an unmodified single-player Creative-mode world. Use a disposable Superflat world so that a full-block cobblestone enclosure can be built and observed without exploration. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start the exact historical release Minecraft 1.4.2, which is the first version in the report's affected-version list.
Do not use either listed fix version, Minecraft 15w45a or Minecraft 17w47a, for this reproduction.
Use the unmodified game without mods that alter entity movement, entity collision, chunk loading, or saving.
The executor must be able to create a single-player world in Creative mode and use the Creative inventory.
Keep the test world available after leaving it; the same saved world must be reopened rather than replaced with another world.

steps.action: Launch the launcher installation configured for the exact release Minecraft 1.4.2, and wait for the game's main menu to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version text on the main menu identifies Minecraft 1.4.2, and the Singleplayer button is usable.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list.
steps.exact_input: Click "Singleplayer".
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is displayed.

steps.action: Begin creating a new disposable test world.
steps.exact_input: Click "Create New World".
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is displayed.

steps.action: Give the world a recognizable name so that the same save can be selected after quitting.
steps.exact_input: Enter "MC-2025 Reproduction" in the world-name field.
steps.success_cue: The world-name field reads "MC-2025 Reproduction".

steps.action: Change the world game mode to Creative so the enclosure and chickens can be created without crafting or exploration.
steps.exact_input: Click the Game Mode button until it displays "Game Mode: Creative".
steps.success_cue: The creation screen explicitly shows Creative mode.

steps.action: Open the additional world settings and select the Superflat world type, using the world-type button repeatedly if necessary.
steps.exact_input: Click "More World Options...", then click the World Type button until it displays "World Type: Superflat".
steps.success_cue: The world type is displayed as Superflat.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until initial terrain generation and player movement have finished loading.
steps.exact_input: Click "Create New World".
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: Press E using the default controls.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and item tabs are visible.

steps.action: Locate the full cobblestone building block, not a cobblestone wall item, and place a stack in an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: A stack of ordinary full-block cobblestone is present in the hotbar.

steps.action: Locate the spawn egg whose tooltip identifies that it spawns a chicken, and place it in a different hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A chicken-spawning egg is present in the hotbar alongside the cobblestone.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory and select the hotbar slot containing cobblestone.
steps.exact_input: Press E, then press the number key corresponding to the cobblestone hotbar slot or use the mouse wheel to select it.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, cobblestone is shown in the player's hand, and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Build a level 8-by-8 floor made entirely from full cobblestone blocks. Keep all floor blocks at the same Y level.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place each cobblestone block.
steps.success_cue: A complete solid 8-by-8 cobblestone floor is present with no holes.

steps.action: Build a two-block-high cobblestone wall around the entire outer perimeter of the 8-by-8 floor. Place the first wall layer on top of the floor's perimeter blocks and the second wall layer directly above it. Leave the top open and do not add a doorway. This creates a 6-by-6 interior with two blocks of vertical clearance.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place cobblestone around the perimeter, then repeat directly above the first perimeter layer.
steps.success_cue: The enclosure has a solid 6-by-6 interior floor, an unbroken two-full-block-high cobblestone perimeter, and an open top.

steps.action: Move into or hover directly above the enclosure, then select the hotbar slot containing the chicken-spawning egg.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the chicken spawn egg or use the mouse wheel to select it.
steps.success_cue: The chicken-spawning egg is in the player's hand and the crosshair can target the enclosure's interior floor.

steps.action: Spawn exactly 10 chickens inside the enclosure, distributing the clicks over the interior floor so that every chicken appears inside the walls.
steps.exact_input: Right-click an interior floor block 10 times in total.
steps.success_cue: Ten chickens are present inside the enclosure, with none intentionally spawned on top of or outside the perimeter.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that subsequent clicks or movement do not spawn additional chickens or place blocks.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key for an empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty and neither cobblestone nor the spawn egg is held.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight and hover over the center of the enclosure, approximately four to six blocks above its interior floor, while looking down at the chickens.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space to begin flying; use Space to rise and the movement controls to center over the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary above the open enclosure and all or most of its interior can be seen without the player physically pushing the chickens.

steps.action: Allow the chickens to move naturally for up to five minutes while watching for at least one chicken to gather against an inside wall or corner. Continue as soon as a chicken is pressed tightly against the inside face of a cobblestone wall; do not wait the full five minutes if that state is reached earlier.
steps.success_cue: At least one chicken is visibly touching or pressed tightly against the inner face or corner of the cobblestone wall.

steps.action: If no chicken becomes tightly wall-adjacent during the waiting period, descend into the enclosure and gently herd several chickens toward the same inside corner by walking slowly behind them. Use only player-body collision: do not left-click, attack, sprint, place blocks, or remove blocks. If step 18 already achieved the required wall-adjacent state, make no input and proceed.
steps.exact_input: Use the normal movement keys, including W as needed; do not left-click.
steps.success_cue: At least one living chicken is pressed tightly against the inner face or corner of the solid cobblestone wall, and the enclosure remains intact.

steps.action: Move back above the enclosure in Creative flight and verify that at least one chicken is still adjacent to an inside wall or corner. Keep the enclosure in view so that the same area will be immediately visible after reloading.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space if flight was exited, then use Space and the movement controls to hover over the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering above the enclosure, the enclosure is visible below, and at least one chicken remains against an inside wall or corner.

steps.action: Save the current entity positions and leave the world while the chickens are in this wall-adjacent arrangement.
steps.exact_input: Press Esc, then click "Save and Quit to Title".
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed, confirming that the test world has been saved and closed.

steps.action: Return to the single-player world list.
steps.exact_input: Click "Singleplayer".
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is displayed and the saved "MC-2025 Reproduction" world is listed.

steps.action: Select the same saved test world; do not create a replacement world.
steps.exact_input: Click the world named "MC-2025 Reproduction" once.
steps.success_cue: The "MC-2025 Reproduction" entry is highlighted as the world that will be loaded.

steps.action: Load the selected saved world once. This is the trigger action because it reloads the chunk containing the saved, wall-adjacent chickens.
steps.exact_input: Click "Play Selected" or double-click the highlighted "MC-2025 Reproduction" world entry.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen transitions back to gameplay in the same saved world.

steps.action: Make no movement or interaction input after entering the world. Wait only until the enclosure and chickens have rendered sufficiently for observation; do not perform another save-and-reload cycle before handing off.
steps.success_cue: The saved enclosure and its chickens are visible, the chunk has rendered, and the player has not moved or interacted since the world opened.

stor.handoff_condition: The same saved Minecraft 1.4.2 world has just been reopened once, the chunk containing the solid cobblestone enclosure has rendered, and the player remains positioned to view the chickens without making post-load movement or interaction inputs. Begin observing the chickens' positions and state relative to the enclosure walls.
uncertainties: The report has no single formal Steps to Reproduce section. This plan reconstructs the minimum path primarily from Comment 54, which specifies a 6x6x2 cobblestone/stone room, approximately 10 chickens, closing the map, and loading the map, with support from Comments 56 and 100 describing save-and-reload reproduction.

The phrase "6x6x2 room" is interpreted as a 6-by-6 interior enclosed by two-block-high full cobblestone walls with an open top. The report does not explicitly state whether those dimensions include the wall thickness.

The issue is described as probabilistic. Some comments recommend reloading multiple times, but this plan performs only one load trigger and hands off immediately, in accordance with the requirement not to repeat a trigger merely to exaggerate the issue.

The optional gentle herding step is a practical method for establishing the report's stated condition that a mob is directly next to or partly pressing into a block before saving. It is not asserted as a mandatory cause by the report.

The report covers many mobs and enclosure materials. Chickens and full cobblestone blocks were selected because Comment 54 supplies that specific reproduction variant; cobblestone wall blocks and wooden fences are not used in this variant.

Use a regular Item Frame in the recommended version. Glow Item Frames do not exist in Minecraft 1.7.1, so the glow variant requires a later listed affected version.
Perform the test against a vertical wall made from ordinary solid full blocks; this plan uses Stone as a deterministic practical choice.

The instructions refer to the default controls E for inventory, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, left-click for Attack/Destroy, and F3+B for entity hitboxes. If controls are rebound, use the bindings assigned to those actions.

steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab, represented by a compass icon, to locate Stone, Item Frame, and Empty Map. Move at least nine Stone blocks, one Item Frame, and one Empty Map into separate hotbar slots. Keep one other hotbar slot empty, then press E again to close the inventory.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition Minecraft 1.8.4, preferably an unmodified single-player client. Use a newly created Creative-mode world as a practical setup convenience. The reproduction uses one adult tamed and saddled horse, an Overworld-to-Nether linked portal pair, and standard portals whose active interior is 2 blocks wide by 3 blocks high. No particular world seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version Minecraft 1.8.4 rather than a fix version.
Use a world in which Nether travel is available. Creative mode is selected only to obtain the horse and portal materials deterministically; the report does not require Creative mode.
Keep the portal approach level and accessible so the horse can be ridden straight into the active portal blocks.
Use the standard portal dimensions described in the report: a 2-block-wide by 3-block-high active portal opening, surrounded by its obsidian frame.

The destination portal must already exist and its surrounding terrain must be loaded before transporting the horse. This avoids mixing initial destination generation delays with the final trigger sequence.
Use an adult horse. If the Spawn Horse item produces a foal, spawn another horse and use an adult.
Use the default controls described below, or substitute the executor's corresponding rebound controls: E for inventory, W for forward movement, right-click for use/mount, and Left Shift for dismount.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that runs Java Edition version 1.8.4, start it, and wait for the main menu to appear. Confirm that the displayed game version is 1.8.4 before continuing.
steps.exact_input: Launcher version/installation: 1.8.4
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.8.4 main menu is open.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, and create the world. The report does not require a particular seed, so leave the seed unspecified. Wait until terrain has rendered and normal movement is responsive.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Overworld in Creative mode and can move normally.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to locate Obsidian, Flint and Steel, Spawn Horse, and Saddle. Place each item in the player inventory or hotbar, then close the inventory with E. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; an item is selected when its slot has the highlighted outline.
steps.exact_input: E; item names: Obsidian, Flint and Steel, Spawn Horse, Saddle; E
steps.success_cue: Obsidian, Flint and Steel, Spawn Horse, and Saddle are available in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Find a reasonably flat Overworld location with enough room to ride a horse straight toward the portal. Build a vertical obsidian frame with an active interior cavity exactly 2 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. For an easy full-corner frame, place 4 obsidian blocks across the bottom, construct a 5-block-high pillar at each end, and connect the pillars with 4 obsidian blocks across the top. This produces a 4-by-5 outer frame around the required 2-by-3 interior.
steps.exact_input: Portal interior: 2 blocks wide x 3 blocks high; full outer frame: 4 blocks wide x 5 blocks high
steps.success_cue: A complete upright obsidian frame surrounds an empty interior that is 2 blocks wide and 3 blocks high.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the hotbar. Stand facing the inside of the frame and right-click the exposed upper face of either bottom obsidian block inside the opening to ignite the portal.
steps.exact_input: Select Flint and Steel; right-click inside the obsidian frame
steps.success_cue: The 2-by-3 interior of the frame is filled with animated purple portal blocks.

steps.action: Before transporting the horse, enter the portal alone to generate or load its Nether destination. Walk into the purple portal field and remain inside it without stepping out until the dimension transition occurs. After arriving, wait until the Nether terrain and destination portal have rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: W into the portal; remain in the purple portal field until transported
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether beside a loaded destination portal and can move normally.

steps.action: Inspect the destination portal without changing its width. Confirm that it has the standard active opening of 2 portal blocks wide by 3 portal blocks high. If immediately adjacent terrain prevents the player from entering or leaving through either face, remove only enough non-frame terrain to make the portal usable; do not remove obsidian, widen the opening, or replace the portal with a larger design.
steps.exact_input: Confirm active portal opening: 2 blocks wide x 3 blocks high
steps.success_cue: The destination portal remains a standard 2-by-3 portal and can be entered from at least one face.

steps.action: Use the destination portal to return to the Overworld. Enter its purple field and remain there until transported. Wait after arrival until the Overworld terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: W into the Nether-side portal; remain inside until transported
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the loaded Overworld beside the original standard portal.

steps.action: Move several blocks away from the portal so the horse will not touch it prematurely. Select Spawn Horse in the hotbar and right-click the ground to create a horse. Use an adult horse; if a foal appears, spawn another horse until an adult is available.
steps.exact_input: Select Spawn Horse; right-click the ground
steps.success_cue: An adult horse is standing in the Overworld near, but not inside, the portal.

steps.action: Tame the adult horse. Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is not holding an item, face the horse, and right-click it to mount. If the horse throws the player off, approach and right-click it again. Repeat until the horse accepts the player; the successful taming event is indicated by heart particles and the horse no longer immediately throwing the player off.
steps.exact_input: Select an empty hotbar slot; repeatedly right-click the adult horse as needed
steps.success_cue: Heart particles have appeared and the player can remain mounted on the tamed horse.

steps.action: While mounted on the tamed horse, press E to open the horse inventory. Move the Saddle from the player inventory into the horse's saddle slot beside the horse illustration, then press E to close the interface.
steps.exact_input: E; move Saddle to the horse's saddle slot; E
steps.success_cue: The horse visibly wears a saddle, the inventory interface is closed, and the player remains mounted with directional control of the horse.

steps.action: While mounted, position the horse on level ground directly in front of the Overworld portal. Face the center of the 2-block-wide opening so that riding straight forward will place the horse between the two vertical obsidian sides rather than against one side. Stop before the horse touches the purple portal field.
steps.exact_input: Movement controls as needed; face the center of the portal opening
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is aligned with the center of the standard portal and has a clear straight path into it.

steps.action: Hold W to ride the horse straight into the active purple portal blocks. Continue only until the horse's body occupies the portal plane; do not turn sideways or deliberately steer into the obsidian frame.
steps.exact_input: Hold W
steps.success_cue: The horse and rider are positioned within the active portal field while still in the Overworld.

steps.action: Press the dismount control, Left Shift by default, while the horse is still within the active portal field. After dismounting, avoid walking into or pushing the horse while waiting for its entity transfer.
steps.exact_input: Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The player is standing beside the portal, is no longer mounted, and the horse remains in contact with the active portal field.

steps.action: Wait for the horse to pass through the portal, indicated by the horse disappearing from the Overworld. If it walks completely out of the purple field before disappearing, remount it and repeat the alignment, entry, and dismount sequence from steps 12 through 14. Once the horse disappears, do not perform unrelated actions before following it.
steps.success_cue: The horse has disappeared from the Overworld through the active portal while the player remains beside the portal.

steps.action: Immediately follow the horse through the same portal. Walk straight into the purple portal field and remain there until the player is transported to the Nether. As soon as the destination terrain renders and controls respond, do not walk, jump, mount, push, strike, or otherwise reposition the horse; hand control to the observation subsystem at that point.
steps.exact_input: W into the portal; remain in the portal field until the Nether loads
steps.success_cue: The player has just materialized at the loaded Nether-side standard portal immediately after the horse, with no post-arrival movement or interaction performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The horse has been sent through the standard 2-by-3 portal, and the player has just followed it and materialized at the loaded Nether-side portal. Begin observation immediately, before moving the player or interacting with the horse or portal.
uncertainties: The report contains no single formal top-level Steps to Reproduce section. The selected sequence is reconstructed primarily from comment 4: tame a horse, ride into a standard portal, dismount so the horse teleports, and then enter the portal after it.

Minecraft 1.8.4 is selected because it is the first listed affected version, as required. The strongest explicit claims of near-100-percent reproduction with standard portals are attached to 1.9 pre-releases and later versions, so the exact reproduction frequency in 1.8.4 is not quantified by the supplied text.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or a required single-player versus dedicated-server environment. A new single-player Creative world is used as a practical deterministic setup.

Creative mode, Creative inventory acquisition, pre-generating the destination portal, and clearing only terrain that makes the destination portal unusable are practical setup choices rather than explicit report requirements.

The report discusses more than one possible portal collision path: initial destination placement intersecting a frame or nearby wall, and the following player pushing the horse toward the frame. This plan preserves the reported order that can exercise both paths, but it does not add a surrounding wall or use mismatched portal widths.
The report says the issue can occur in both Overworld-to-Nether and Nether-to-Overworld travel. This plan uses only Overworld-to-Nether travel as the minimum supported reproduction path.
Portal transition and chunk-loading times depend on machine performance, so readiness is defined by observable loading and control-response cues rather than fixed delays.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition Snapshot 13w06a in a single-player world. Use Creative mode as a practical way to obtain cobblestone and eggs; the report itself does not require a particular game mode. Keep the enclosure's chunk loaded and the single-player game unpaused while the chickens age.
preconditions: Configure the launcher to run the exact affected version Snapshot 13w06a, not a later release or either listed fix version.
Use a world where a small level construction area is available and remains loaded for the entire test.
Use solid cobblestone for the enclosure. Do not substitute transparent or partial barriers such as glass or fences, because the report describes those as a separate pass-through variant.
Have enough inventory space for Cobblestone and Egg items.
Use the default interaction control, right-click, to place blocks and throw eggs unless controls have been rebound.
Once four chicks are present, do not pause the single-player game, leave the area, unload the chunk, replace blocks, push the chickens manually, or add more chickens.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, configure and start the exact historical Java Edition version listed as the first affected version: Snapshot 13w06a.
steps.exact_input: Snapshot 13w06a
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reaches the title screen and identifies the running version as 13w06a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a fresh world in Creative mode. Creative mode is selected only to make acquiring the required blocks and eggs deterministic; no cheats or commands are needed.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative single-player world and can place blocks without collecting resources.

steps.action: Move to a clear, level area with enough room to build and view a small enclosure. Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally before building.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The player is standing beside a loaded, level construction area with no existing blocks obstructing the enclosure.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory control, whose default key is E. Locate Cobblestone and place a stack into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: A Cobblestone stack is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing Cobblestone, using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar number key 1-9 corresponding to Cobblestone
steps.success_cue: Cobblestone is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Place one cobblestone block to serve as the floor of the enclosure. Keep track of this block as the single interior floor position.
steps.exact_input: Right-click
steps.success_cue: One cobblestone floor block is present at the chosen test position.

steps.action: Around the four horizontal sides of the floor position, build solid cobblestone walls. Each side wall must extend two blocks vertically above the floor surface. Leave the central 1-by-1 air column empty and leave the top open so eggs can be thrown into it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place each Cobblestone block
steps.success_cue: The construction has a one-block-wide interior, two blocks of interior height, four solid cobblestone sides, a solid floor, and an open top.

steps.action: Inspect the enclosure from above and from each accessible side. Confirm there are no gaps in the four walls and that every wall block is full cobblestone rather than glass, fence, slab, or another non-solid substitute.
steps.success_cue: The only exit from the 1-by-1 interior is through the open top, and all four side walls are solid cobblestone and two blocks high.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory again. Locate the item named Egg and place a stack into a hotbar slot.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: An Egg stack is visible in the hotbar while the cobblestone enclosure remains intact.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing the eggs.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar number key 1-9 corresponding to Egg
steps.success_cue: An egg is shown in the player's hand and the Egg hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Stand beside or above the enclosure and aim the crosshair downward at the cobblestone floor inside the central 1-by-1 space. Do not enter or alter the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points into the enclosure so a thrown egg will impact inside it rather than outside it.

steps.action: Throw one egg into the enclosure with the use-item control, whose default input is right-click. Wait for that egg to impact before throwing another.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once
steps.success_cue: The egg has broken inside the enclosure; either no chick appeared or one or more baby chickens are visibly confined inside.

steps.action: Count the baby chickens currently inside after each impact. If fewer than four are present, repeat steps 11 and 12 one egg at a time. Stop throwing eggs as soon as exactly four baby chickens are simultaneously present. Because egg hatching is random, many eggs may be required. If a rare multi-chick hatch causes the total to jump above four, discard that attempt and repeat in a fresh enclosure so the aging phase begins with exactly four.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once per egg
steps.success_cue: Exactly four small, baby-sized chickens are visible inside the enclosure, and no adult chicken is present.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot or a non-egg item so no additional eggs are thrown accidentally. Move to a viewing position immediately outside the enclosure where all four chicks can be monitored without touching or pushing them.

steps.action: Allow the four chickens to age naturally. Keep the game running, remain close enough that the enclosure stays loaded, and do not open the pause menu. Watch continuously until the first chick visibly changes from the smaller baby form to the full-size adult form. The growth transition while confined next to the solid cobblestone walls is the trigger action for observation.
steps.success_cue: At least one of the original four egg-spawned chickens has just completed its visible baby-to-adult size transition while the enclosure remains unchanged and loaded.

stor.handoff_condition: The first of the four egg-spawned chicks has just changed to adult size inside the unchanged 1-by-1, two-block-high solid cobblestone enclosure. Keep the world unpaused and the chunk loaded, make no further player interactions with the chickens or enclosure, and hand control to the observation subsystem for the remainder of the chickens' maturation and the report's final count.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected as a practical implementation choice for obtaining cobblestone and enough eggs without adding unrelated resource gathering.

The phrase "one block large, two block high enclosure" is interpreted as a 1-by-1 interior floor space surrounded on all four sides by full solid walls extending two blocks above the floor, with the top left open for throwing eggs.
Chicken hatching from thrown eggs is random. The plan therefore uses repeated single throws and requires a fresh attempt if a multi-chick hatch causes the initial population to exceed four.
The report provides no exact natural-growth duration. The plan uses the visible baby-to-adult model transition as the readiness and trigger cue rather than assuming a timer.
